peers.name: emil-design-eng
peers.description: Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy for UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great. Use when building or reviewing a UI component's interactions and polish (press and hover states, popover origin, tooltip timing, transitions vs keyframes, clip-path techniques, drag details) and no narrower skill fits.

peers.name: review-animations
peers.description: Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

peers.name: apple-design
peers.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.

peers.name: animation-vocabulary
peers.description: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.

en.tagline: Find the right skill for a UI or motion task
en.summary: Ask Emil is a router for the skills in this repo. You describe your situation, and it recommends one skill or a short sequence, with a reason and the next skill to reach for. It reads each skill's SKILL.md before recommending it, because the summaries are for orientation only.
problem: The skills in this repo cover a lot: building UI, animating, gesture work, finding breakage, reviewing motion, and auditing existing code. It is hard to tell which one fits a given problem. Without a router, you guess or read the files yourself.
With ask-emil, you describe the situation in plain words, such as 'it stutters' or 'it doesn't follow my finger'. You get one starting skill and the reason for it.
fit: You know the problem but not the skill name.
You want one clear next step for a UI or motion task.
You can't tell if the motion is bad, missing, or too much.
unfit: You already know which skill you need. Call it directly.
The task falls outside the skills in this repo.
steps: The user describes the situation in their own words, such as 'it stutters' or 'animate this'.
Before recommending anything, the router reads the SKILL.md of the skills it might suggest.
It picks one skill, or one short sequence, that fits the situation.
It states the reason in one sentence.
It names the skill to reach for next, without listing the whole map.

zh.tagline: 为界面和动效任务找到合适的技能
zh.summary: Ask Emil 是本仓库技能的路由器。你描述当前情况，它会推荐一个技能或一小段流程，并说明理由和下一步该用的技能。推荐前，它会先读取对应技能的 SKILL.md，因为仓库里的简介只用于大致了解。
problem: 本仓库的技能覆盖很多方面：搭建界面、做动效、手势交互、排查问题、审查动效和检查现有代码。一个问题到底该用哪个技能，并不容易判断。没有路由器时，只能凭猜测，或者自己去翻文件。
使用 ask-emil 时，你只需用平常的话描述情况，比如“它会卡顿”或“它没有跟着我的手指走”。它会给出一个起点技能，并说明为什么选它。
fit: 知道问题是什么，但不知道该用哪个技能。
想为界面或动效任务找一个明确的下一步。
拿不准动效是效果不好、缺少动效，还是动效太多。
unfit: 已经清楚要用哪个技能，直接调用即可。
任务不在本仓库技能的范围内。
steps: 用户用自己的话描述情况，比如“它会卡顿”或“帮我加个动画”。
推荐之前，路由器会先读取可能相关技能的 SKILL.md。
从中选出一个技能，或一小段合适的流程。
用一句话说明选择的理由。
指出接下来该用的技能，不把整张技能表列出来。
